title: Asymmetric binary Bose mixtures: a Functional Renormalisation Group study
abstract: Zero-temperature binary Bose mixtures with mass and intraspecies couplings imbalances are studied using the functional renormalisation group (FRG) framework. We find that this dual asymmetry induces a spontaneous redistribution of quantum fluctuations between the components. This effect leads to a significant divergence in the quasiparticle residues of the two species, a phenomenon not captured in mean-field treatments. Critically, our FRG analysis predicts a systematic reduction of the density-channel sound velocity with increasing asymmetry -- a result that qualitatively contradicts the behaviour predicted by standard Bogoliubov theory. The ratio of the renormalisation factors is proposed as a robust quantitative probe of many-body correlations and fluctuation transfer. These findings provide a consistent non-perturbative framework for interpreting future experiments on heterogeneous mixtures.
summary: This paper uses the Functional Renormalisation Group to study asymmetric binary Bose mixtures at zero temperature. It demonstrates that mass imbalance drives a spontaneous redistribution of quantum fluctuations, causing measurable deviations from simple mean-field predictions. The key finding is the systematic reduction of the density sound velocity due to these non-perturbative correlation effects.
main_problem: The study investigates zero-temperature binary Bose mixtures exhibiting mass and intraspecies coupling imbalances.
main_result: The analysis shows that dual asymmetry causes a spontaneous redistribution of quantum fluctuations, leading to quasiparticle residue divergences and systematically reducing the density-channel sound velocity contrary to standard Bogoliubov theory.
method: The Functional Renormalisation Group (FRG) framework is employed to provide a non-perturbative treatment of many-body correlations beyond mean-field approximations.
model_or_system: The system models binary Bose mixtures ($\phi$ and $\psi$) with tunable mass imbalances ($R=m_1/m_2$) and interspecies coupling ($\gamma$). The analysis focuses on collective excitations like density and spin sound modes.
key_observables: Quasiparticle residues, density-channel sound velocity ($c_+$), spin-channel sound velocity ($c_-$), and the ratio of renormalization factors ($\sigma = Z_2/Z_1 - 1$).
important_parameters: Mass asymmetry factor ($R$), interspecies coupling constant ($\gamma_{st}$), and intraspecies coupling ratios ($s =  eta_2/ eta_1$). The analysis is restricted to the dilute regime ($n a^3 \ll 1$).
main_assumptions: The FRG calculation relies on specific truncations of the effective action ansatz, which are assumed reliable in the dilute gas limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how sound velocities decrease with increasing mass asymmetry ($R$), and show the evolution of the relative dynamical renormalization ($\sigma$) as a function of coupling strengths.
paper_structure: The paper develops the FRG flow equations for the effective action, analyzes the impact of asymmetry on quasiparticle residues, and compares the resulting predictions for sound velocities against established Bogoliubov theory.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, non-perturbative tool (FRG) to quantify how quantum fluctuations modify collective excitations in multicomponent ultracold atomic mixtures, offering crucial corrections over standard mean-field models.
